summary: Replaces AL-1's fixed linear-dB release with a 3-stage program-adaptive release: hold → fast (transient) → slow (sustained). Architecture from Weiss DS1 MK3 hardware (public literature). Lookahead/attack path UNCHANGED.

stages.description: RMS averaging window over the input signal — detects sustained content vs short transients. Output: sustained_factor ∈ [0,1].

behavior_targets.description: Single short transient (1ms click, −6 dBFS): sustained_factor must remain <0.1 throughout entire event
behavior_targets.signal: 1ms impulse at −6 dBFS, silence before/after (100ms window)

behavior_targets.description: Sustained loud tone (1kHz sine, 500ms, −6 dBFS): sustained_factor must rise to >0.9 after ≥Average_ms ms
Transition: sustained_factor changes smoothly (no hard step) when content transitions transient→sustained or vice versa

null_test.oracle: synthetic_analytical: compute expected RMS over window of length Average_samples directly from input signal
null_test.signal: sweep: silence + click + silence + tone + silence at −6 dBFS

literature: Zölzer DAFX 2nd ed. ch.4 — RMS detector (boxcar window: running-sum ring buffer Σx²/N)
Giannoulis et al. 2012 JAES — detector structures for dynamic range control
stages.implementation_note: RMS detector = ring buffer of squared samples, sum maintained incrementally. Length = Average_ms × fs. Normalized to [0,1] against a reference level (e.g. threshold). sustained_factor = clamp((rms_db - (threshold - knee)) / knee, 0, 1). Compute on the PRE-gain-reduction signal, NOT the output.

stages.description: After peak GR is reached, hold GR constant for Release_Delay_ms before starting release. Prevents premature release on consecutive peaks.

behavior_targets.description: After a peak event, GR must NOT decrease for exactly Release_Delay_ms samples, then begin releasing
behavior_targets.signal: single 1ms burst at −3 dBFS, silence after

behavior_targets.description: If a new peak occurs during hold, hold timer resets (GR stays at new max, delay restarts)

null_test.oracle: synthetic_analytical: GR envelope must be flat for exactly floor(Release_Delay_ms × fs / 1000) samples after peak

literature: Bohn & Hearst 2000 — 'Dynamic Processors — Technology & Techniques', hold time in compressor design
stages.implementation_note: Hold counter: decrement each sample after GR peak reached. Release only allowed when hold_counter == 0. On any new peak (GR increases), reset hold_counter = Release_Delay_samples. When Release_Delay = 0, stage is a no-op.

stages.description: Dual one-pole release smoother: blend between fast τ and slow τ based on sustained_factor from stage 1. Smooth blend avoids discontinuity on bucket switch.

behavior_targets.description: After single 1ms transient (sustained_factor→0): GR must release at approximately exp-decay with τ=Release_Fast_ms (±20%)
behavior_targets.signal: 1ms burst at −6 dBFS, Release_Fast=20ms, Release_Slow=500ms, Average=50ms

behavior_targets.description: After 500ms sustained tone (sustained_factor→1): GR must release at approximately exp-decay with τ=Release_Slow_ms (±20%)
Blend continuity: NO discontinuity or click when sustained_factor transitions. Release rate changes smoothly.

Backward compat: when Release_Fast = Release_Slow = AL-1 release rate equivalent (0.272 dB/sample linear), output must null against AL-1 ≤−60 dB (linear-dB vs one-pole are different shapes — this tests parameter-space boundary only; full shape match NOT required)
behavior_targets.signal: single peak at −6 dBFS, all Release_Delay=0

null_test.oracle: al1_sysid.py (AL-1 black-box harness): when Release_Fast=Release_Slow=AL1_equivalent, verify GR envelope shape matches within envelope tolerance; separate: analytical verification of τ=Release_Fast on isolated transient

literature: Zölzer DAFX 2nd ed. ch.4 — one-pole smoother: a = 1 − exp(−1/(τ·fs)); asymmetric attack/release
Giannoulis et al. 2012 JAES — smooth-decoupled branch design for dynamic processors
McNally 1984 JAES — 'Dynamic Range Control of Digital Audio Signals' — dual-release concept
stages.implementation_note: a_fast = 1 − exp(−1/(Release_Fast_ms × fs / 1000)); a_slow = 1 − exp(−1/(Release_Slow_ms × fs / 1000)); a_blend = lerp(a_fast, a_slow, sustained_factor). GR_db[n] = max(0, GR_db[n-1] × (1 − a_blend)). Note: one-pole in dB domain = exponential decay in dB = different shape from AL-1's linear-dB. ES-L voicing decision: use one-pole (smoother tail) OR keep linear-dB for fast bucket only (see voicing below).
stages.voicing: Option A (Weiss-style): both fast+slow as one-pole τ — smooth tails, classic mastering feel. Option B (Hybrid): fast bucket = linear-dB (AL-1 style, punchy), slow bucket = one-pole τ (smooth). Option A recommended for mastering context.
excluded_ref: DS1-MK3 exact release curve shape (iLok blocked — not measured)
DS1-MK3 sustained_factor blend function (not measured — analytical design used instead)

params_added.name: average_ms
params_added.note: RMS window for bucket decision; 0 = always fast

signal_chain_patch: AL-1 unchanged EXCEPT: after 'GR_db = max(0, GR_prev − relRate)', replace relRate with: hold_delay stage → blended_release stage. Lookahead (PURE-MAX combine + phi slew) UNTOUCHED.
risks: One-pole vs linear-dB shape: outputs will NOT null-test perfectly against AL-1 by design (different release shapes). This is intentional — ES-L sounds different from AL-1 with 3-bucket enabled.
sustained_factor computation adds latency of Average_ms to the 'feel' of bucket switching — set Average_ms ≥ 20ms to avoid jitter on bucket selection.
If Release_Slow >> Release_Fast and sustained_factor oscillates, GR can have visible low-frequency modulation. Guard: one-pole filter on sustained_factor itself (τ≈20ms).
